text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games has called on the gederal government to defer the closure of Telstra's analog mobile phone network until after the Games in the year 2000 to prevent communications mayhem. The Committee warned that Australia could face international embarrassment if the government closed the analog network just nine months before the Olympics. Page 3.

The economic outlook, the republic issue and the High Court's Wik native title decision will be on the agenda when federal cabinet meets for the first time this year. The mid-year economic review, presented by Treasurer Peter Costello, is expected to show lower than expected inflation and wages outlooks. The government is still consulting over a response to the Wik native title decision and there is increasing pressure for a plebiscite on the republic issue. Page 2.

Market economists predict the gederal government's mid-year budget review will show improved inflation outlook but slow jobs growth. The review, which sets the economic parameters to be used in the 1997/98 budget, may also show a targeted 3.5 percent economic growth rate but the underlying deficit may be A$1 billion higher than predicted due to Senate's obstruction of some parts of the 1996/97 budget. Page 2.

Businesses may already be preparing for the introduction of a goods and services tax, according to Cooper and Lybrand's indirect taxes partner, Alan Smolak. Despite federal government denials of such a tax being on the agenda, Mr Smolak says businesses are including in contracts clauses dealing with such a change to the tax system. Mr Smolak says a GST could have a significant impact in the area of pricing. Page 4.

A new study by the Australian Council for Educational Research has found fewer students from poor and rural backgrounds are completing Year 12, indicating a widening of the social gap in school retention rates since the beginning of the decade. The study found many students left school before completing Year 12 because they saw no point in continuing secondary education. Page 1.

An investigation by The Australian has revealed Australia's massive casino industry is facing turmoil as nine of the country's 14 legal gambling houses face a profit slump or ownership changes. Industry experts are warning that the casino market in Australia is saturated as pressure is placed on state government's to ease tax rates on casinos to protect long-term revenue. Page 1.

A married couple were killed as Melbourne's freakish summer weather turned lethal yesterday. They were struck by lightning in front of family members while picnicking at a park in Geelong. The couple's two children witnessed the lightning strike which killed the 39-year-old woman instantly, and caused the man, 42, to die on the way to hospital. Page 1.

NSW Opposition leader Peter Collins has warned any delay in a people's convention on a republic could be politically damaging for the federal government. Mr Collins called on Prime Minister John Howard to set a timetable to debate the issue as the Ausralian community is beginning to "lose patience" over gederal inaction. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Under controversial changes to be put to the federal government within the next few months, political parties and candidates could be fined for publishing misleading material during election campaigns. It is to be proposed that "inaccurate statements of fact" in political advertising would be monitored by an independent agency other than the Australian Electoral Commission. Page 1.

A scathing report by the Community Services Commission claims that an institution for intellectually disabled children in the Blue Mountains, west of Sydney, poses a serious risk to its 60 residents and their safety cannot be guaranteed at the institution. The report outlines frequent sexual assault of female residents due to poor supervision and inadequate staff numbers. Page 1.

In a move which will see the federal government fail to deliver a central election promise to remove political interference from its economic forecasts by having the Reserve Bank join the Treasury in producing "independent" economic assessments, Treasurer Peter Costello is believed to have instructed the Reserve Bank to scrap the publication of independent forecasts for the economy. Page 3.

A confidential draft report to the NSW Education Minister John Aquilina reveals teachers' computer abilities are failing to meet the growing demands of schools and students and recommends the state's teachers will need more training in key areas to cope wth the technology revolution in the classroom. Page 3.
THE AGE

Sales figures from November indicate Melbourne will soon have Australia's second highest median house prices. The second of three interest cuts in 1996 encouraged buyers, with prices consistently rising in 1996. Melbourne prices are slightly below Canberra's, with Sydney being in top spot. Page 1.

Two people were killed when a bolt of lightening hit a tin-roofed rotunda where they were sheltering in Geelong, Victoria yesterday. The husband and wife were with friends from a local church when the lightning struck at about 9.10 a.m. A 42-year-old woman also suffered a respiratory arrest in the strike but was revived and two men and a woman aged in their 40s and 50s were admitted to hospital suffering from shock. Page 1.

A new loyalty programme, Advantage Australia, to be launched in March in a A$10 million campaign, will offer reward stamps to shoppers who buy a product from one of 120 participating companies, a move which may help reduce Australia's current account deficit. Page 1.

A survey by the Australian Council of Deans of Education has predicted an acute teacher shortage in Victoria within six years. The survey says Victorian policy of allowing schools to choose teachers in a competitive environment, coupled with massive government cuts in education, will lead to the shortage. The Council says country schools and poorer schools will be hardest hit. Page 3.
